Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: The records office files administrative paperwork: intake forms, access logs, correspondence records, and access-authority documents. Each item carries account identifiers, timestamps, and channel references. Cross-references link documents within a case file.
2) What occurred: The actor submitted an intake form referencing administrative credentials in an institutional network. A draft operational plan document was attached, listing phases for system modification, recovery control, rapid propagation, and payment-pressure measures with attribution-evasion fields. The actor routed the document through a messaging channel and referenced an account with elevated authority. A follow-up message requested scheduling parameters and a named distribution target set.
3) Materials/access observed: An intake form with a request field; an attached planning document with phase, target, and evasion fields; a named account holding administrative-level authority; a channel record showing transmission; dated log entries correlating the account to the submission time.
4) Indicators & artifacts: Intake form ID, attachment hash, account identifier, channel message IDs, submission timestamp, and the phase/target/evasion field values in the planning document.
